nature: A 2026-10-24 BACKFILL (JOB BOARD-SCENES-BACKFILL), stated in the scene's own first decision record (DR-BACKFILL): the piece predates the HTML-SCENE LAW and the board could only offer a YouTube embed, which the owner's phone walls with a bot check. The scene is rebuilt from the piece's own production data — hidden_files/short01-v3/assemble.py's segment table (20 segments with their zoompan moves), its captions.ass (55 timed text events) and its own scene/panel images — so the board plays the production file itself. In the scene's own words: 'Faithful, not modernized: same images, same words, same order, same timings as the published video. The MP4 is NOT re-rendered from this scene.' The original build's renderer (the 2026-10-21 short01-v3 assembly) is NOT this file: this file is the backfill's reconstruction of the published build, and the package says so wherever the scene is described.

in_scene_decisions.summary: The backfill account quoted in nature above: rebuilt 2026-10-24 (JOB BOARD-SCENES-BACKFILL) from the piece's own production data (assemble.py segment table, captions.ass, scene/panel images); faithful, not modernized; the MP4 is not re-rendered from this scene. Its context cites Hadi at Action #34, 2026-10-24: 'still the rendered video from youtube cannot watch. Need html format.'

'The locked final script (files/short-01-agent-harness-final-script.md): the same stack teaching as the Poster version, carried by the assembling board — parts fly in and lock as they are named.' Alternative recorded: the Poster version's cut (published as its deliberate pair). Context: 'Lesson 1 pair verdict is Hadi's (Action #34); both versions published 2026-10-21/22.'

'The build's own images in its own order: fifteen drawn board scenes (scenes/sc00–sc14) and the panel states (panel/state0–5.png), each with the build's measured zoompan move.' Cuts sit on measured silence-detect run starts (its context).

'Reproduced exactly as published: the narration appears in timed chunks (the build's captions.ass events — white DejaVu Sans bold with amber key chunks and cyan labels), each chunk fading in/out on its measured window. This is the proto word-animation form this generation of pieces was published with.' Rebuilding the text as per-word DOM animation was rejected for the backfill (it would change the published piece; modernization belongs to a re-edit). Its context flags the treatment against the WORD-ANIMATION LAW rather than silently changing it.

'The published MP4's own audio track (short-01-agent-harness-final.mp4), re-encoded to MP3 192k — the exact narration + music mix viewers heard, including container intro/outro audio where the wrap added it.' (Here the word 'published' is exact: this piece IS published, unlike the draft pieces whose backfill records borrow the word.)

plan.basis: Counted at this migration from the scene's embedded plan: 50 phrase chunks holding 148 word objects (w / start / cx / cy / size / key / col — starts and display parameters; no word ends, no treatments). The backfill's chunk model does not segment phrases by narration line (every phrase carries line 1), so the plan states no per-line grouping and no word total of its own — the transcript layer keys its lines to the script doc's measured map. The 20 plates are the build's 20 segments; the 55 texts are its captions.ass events.
plan.agreement: The plan's word objects match the delivered transcript token-for-token in sequence (148/148 — transcript/transcript.md). The plan total (52.629 s) vs the render container (52.633 s) vs the plan's own contentEnd (52.644 s) differ by milliseconds of container/plan bookkeeping — stated as measured; no identity is claimed beyond it.

embedded_audio.measured: decoded from the scene's data URI and measured at this migration (JOB MIGRATION-22)
embedded_audio.record: per the in-scene DR-AUDIO: the published MP4's own audio track, re-encoded to MP3 192k — the exact narration + music mix of the published build. The re-encode is mono, as is the published mix itself (audio/audio.json).

board_edition.note: The board's served edition does NOT byte-match the master: identity tested at this migration, does not hold. Both hashes are recorded; the package ships the master.

onset_note: Two timing bases stand on this piece's record and are not harmonised: the script doc's measured map puts L1's speech onset at 2.20 s (silencedetect basis), while the backfill plan's first word object starts at 2.39 s (the build's caption/alignment basis) — a 190 ms difference between bases on the first line. The exceptions ledger's entry #11 (late window-open onsets) was checked directly: it names Ep.2 v4's delivered plan only, and this package asserts no onset verdict for this piece — the difference and its two bases are recorded here for the verification round to probe on the branch bytes.
